clue.text: New e-car dented right in the middle

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A brand-new electric car has already picked up a dent.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'e-car' is ignored: the fodder is just the letters. 'Right' reads as the side of the car, but here it means 'exactly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead centre is the exact middle, so 'right in the middle' describes it.

clue.text: Work, and don't go slowly!

definitions.meaning: the noun: one's profession, a working life
the verb: rush along headlong at full speed

explanation.surface: A boss telling someone to get on with the job, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is a noun for one's working life and a verb for hurtling headlong; the exclamation mark makes the second half an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's line of work, and to career is to move fast, the opposite of going slowly.

clue.text: Burner phone is less operationally tricky to begin with, and not too demanding

indicators.note: take what each word begins with, its first letter

parts.note: first letters of Phone Is Less Operationally Tricky
light work is not too demanding

explanation.surface: Someone praises a disposable 'burner' phone as easy to use and undemanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burner phone' looks like a single thing, a disposable mobile; the words must be split, with 'Burner' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot light is the small flame kept burning in a boiler or cooker, a burner in its own right.

clue.text: Ill-tempered individual thus turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning the word up flips it bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy has shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as 'arrived', but in a down clue it means the letters are written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a bad-tempered, fearsome person.

clue.text: Circular motion helping after the first hints of gout, yes?

indicators.note: the first hint of a word is its opening letter
the helping is placed after those letters

parts.note: first letters of Gout and Yes
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether a second helping of rich food came after the first twinges of gout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyration is movement round and round in a circle.

clue.text: Little case in one truck from Sydney, heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: a ute is the Australian word for a pickup truck

explanation.surface: A small box is carried in a truck from Sydney as it heads up the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but only joins definition to wordplay. An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small decorative case for needles, scissors or toiletries.

clue.text: Small cat bad for asthmatics, in all likelihood

definitions.text: bad for asthmatics, in all likelihood

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat

explanation.surface: A small cat is probably bad news for someone with asthma.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at cat allergies; the definition actually describes polluted air.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoggy air is full of pollution, which is likely to trouble asthmatics.

clue.text: Windows maybe get smeary points when tampered with

indicators.note: tampering with the letters changes their order

explanation.surface: Glass windows pick up smudges when people fiddle with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' is capitalised because it opens the clue, which hides that it is Microsoft's software rather than panes of glass; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Microsoft's Windows is one product of this kind, flagged by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Test incorporating part of major road around a city

indicators.note: the test takes the part into its body

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A driving test that covers part of a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' suggests a driving test, fitting the road, but it is a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A British usage: an orbital road circles a city as a satellite orbits, like the M25 round London.

clue.text: Terrible, second-rate plug

parts.note: B grade is second-rate, below A
a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a shoddy electrical plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like an electrical fitting, but it means a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad and terrible both mean of very poor quality.

clue.text: Upsetting the members of Generation X can be liberating, perhaps

indicators.note: the members are the letters, and upsetting them puts them in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters including the X

explanation.surface: Annoying people born in the 1960s and 70s can feel freeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' reads as people of that generation, but it means the letters of the phrase, X included.
explanation.definitionFit: Exonerating someone frees them from blame, one kind of liberating, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: That person's closer to that one who's next in line

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its final letter

parts.note: an heir is next in line to inherit

explanation.surface: Someone is closer to the throne than someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' reads as 'nearer', but it is the noun: the letter that closes 'that'. 'Their' as a singular possessive is standard for a person of unspecified sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Their can mean belonging to a single person of unstated sex, that person's.

clue.text: Large facility absorbing current debt

indicators.note: the facility takes the current into itself

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A big plant soaking up money it owes.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes in straight after the L. 'Facility' reads as a building, but it means a knack, an ability.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounting sense: on a balance sheet, money owed is listed among the liabilities.

clue.text: Sly agreement mostly not favouring church dignitary

indicators.note: most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: con = against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A cunning deal made against a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sly agreement' reads as a single shady deal, but 'Sly' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman ranking below a bishop.

clue.text: Doctor is truly in a state of isolation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it

explanation.surface: A physician really is cut off from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person, but it is a verb: meddle with the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insularity is being cut off like an island, a state of isolation.

clue.text: Allowing the removal of vital fluid?

definitions.meaning: the old medical practice of drawing off blood

explanation.surface: A question about permitting blood to be taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old medical practice of bloodletting; the question mark admits that 'letting' alone is stretched to mean it.
explanation.definitionFit: To let is to allow, and in medicine letting blood means drawing it off.

clue.text: Burst in … burst in without an up-front excuse, ultimately

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: to interrupt is to burst in on a conversation

indicators.note: take the final letter of each word

parts.note: last letters of aN, up-fronT, excusE, removed from INTERRUPTED

explanation.surface: Someone barges in twice over, without even offering an excuse first.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the definition to a second 'burst in', which is INTERRUPTED; its N, T and E go, leaving I-RRUPTED. 'Up-front' reads as 'in advance' but only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or rush in suddenly.

clue.text: Card game players holding an ace

indicators.note: the players hold AN inside them

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
A = ace on a playing card

explanation.surface: People at a card table, one of whom has an ace in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' reads as card players at the table, but it means the actors in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain instance: canasta is a rummy-family game played with two packs, one kind of card game.

clue.text: As a river starts to surge, everything nearby is consumed

indicators.note: take the start of each following word

parts.note: first letters of Surge Everything Nearby Is Consumed

explanation.surface: A river rises and floods everything around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a mere conjunction opening the sentence, but it is the chemical symbol for arsenic and is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the element arsenic.

clue.text: Hated corporate VIP given an appraisal

parts.note: an exec is a company executive

explanation.surface: An unpopular company boss receives a performance review.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's loathed boss is apt, but 'Hated' is the definition and 'given an appraisal' only builds letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to loathe, so execrated means hated.

clue.text: English flower festival

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A flower show held in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English flower festival' reads as one event, the kind a village holds, but splits into three parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain instance: the Christian feast of the resurrection is one of the church's great festivals.

clue.text: A lot of beer bottles break in the middle

indicators.note: to bottle is to keep something inside
take the centre letter of the word

explanation.surface: A heap of beer bottles cracks apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' reads as a noun, glass containers, but it is a verb: the beer keeps the letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Piles means a large amount, a lot.

clue.text: Alcohol from India in former times

indicators.note: I is placed inside the former times

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drink brought over from India long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a colonial drink, but pastis is French, an aniseed spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Dozy people pay less heed, stupidly

indicators.note: the letters are arranged senselessly

explanation.surface: Drowsy people foolishly stop paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair description of the answer itself, which is why the anagram feels natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually said fondly of someone who can't stay awake or has just woken.

clue.text: Big industry event in old post office

explanation.surface: A trade fair is held in a disused post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a container instruction but only joins definition to wordplay; the two pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a large trade exhibition.

clue.text: Quiet section of posh US hotel

indicators.note: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A peaceful wing of a luxury American hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet section' reads as one phrase, a hotel's calm area, but 'Quiet' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a noun or a command, both mean silence or stillness.

clue.text: Some sexagenarians — after retirement — entered a marathon

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used
to retire is to go back, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Some people in their sixties took up marathon running once they stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' fits sixty-somethings perfectly, which hides its job of sending the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran means competed in a race, as in having entered and run a marathon.

clue.text: Like a certain art style, say. It's ionic, possibly

indicators.note: the letters are one possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: Talk of an art style, followed by a remark about Ionic columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' after the definition, but it is EXPRESS. Expressionism is the early 20th-century style of distorted, emotive painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressionistic means in the manner of Expressionism, a particular art style.
